entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0373: Vulnerability in ammonia
entry.summary: Missing case-insensitive matching for CSS url function
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0373

Missing case-insensitive matching for CSS url function
Reported
October 16, 2026
Issued
October 17, 2026
Package
ammonia (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • format-injection
Keywords
#css #html
Aliases
  • GHSA-x43w-36pp-96g3
References
  • https://github.com/rust-ammonia/ammonia/pull/267
Patched
  • >=4.2.4
  • >=4.1.8, <4.2.0

Description

URL filtering, such as relative URLs and URL scheme limits, is not always applied when CSS sanitization is used.

When the inner URL is quoted, CSS url("") is matched case-sensitively, when it should be matched case-insensitively. As a result, while url("") gets the intended domain name filtering, URL("") does not.

The following example shows how an application needs to be configured to trigger this bug.

let mut builder = Builder::new();
// allow inline styles
builder.filter_style_properties(hashset!["background-image"]);
builder.add_generic_attributes(&["style"]);
// notice that "http" URLs aren't allowed
builder.url_schemes(["cid"].into());

// attacker-controlled, presumably
let cleaned = builder.clean(r#"<div style='background:URL("https://evil.com/ping");'>"#);

// this is the expected result
assert_eq!(String::from(&cleaned), r#"<div style="">ok</p>"#);

// this is the result that the vulnerable version actually gets
assert_eq!(String::from(&cleaned), r#"<div style="background-image:URL("https://evil.com/ping");">ok</p>"#);

This can be used to inject tracking pixels where the application intended to prevent them. It does not allow XSS, and its usefulness for data exfiltration is limited.

This vulnerability was reported by Louis Li.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0365: Vulnerability in negentropy
entry.summary: Remote DoS through unchecked `IdList` allocation in negentropy
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0365

Remote DoS through unchecked IdList allocation in negentropy
Reported
October 14, 2026
Issued
October 17, 2026
Package
negentropy (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#allocation #memory-exhaustion #remote
References

  • https://github.com/nostrdevkit/negentropy/commit/40f7290cbc5755a5ba3190279fbc848a97866280
  • https://github.com/nostrdevkit/negentropy/commit/894a32c0ab9f3efd750b3cf06caee27b3f9c3f12
CVSS Score
7.5 HIGH
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.4.4, <0.5.0
  • >=0.5.2
Unaffected
  • <0.2.0

Description

Summary

The negentropy crate is vulnerable to denial-of-service through an unchecked, peer-controlled ID count in reconciliation messages.

With the std feature enabled, which is the default configuration, a small malformed message can trigger an enormous memory allocation and terminate the application.

Details

When processing an IdList range, the reconciliation parser uses the peer-provided ID count to reserve memory before checking whether the message contains the corresponding IDs:

let mut their_elems: HashSet<Id> =
    HashSet::with_capacity(num_ids as usize);

An attacker can declare an arbitrarily large count without supplying any IDs. The allocation occurs before the parser reaches the ID-reading loop, which would otherwise reject the truncated message.

With Rust's default allocation-error behavior, a failed allocation aborts the process rather than unwinding. Consequently, catch_unwind cannot contain the failure.

Both reconcile and reconcile_with_ids reach the vulnerable parser.

The patched versions validate the count against the remaining message length before allocating:

if num_ids > (query.len() / ID_SIZE) as u64 {
    return Err(Error::ParseEndsPrematurely);
}

Impact

An unauthenticated remote attacker can terminate an application that exposes reconciliation to untrusted peers without additional validation.

For example, a Nostr relay that forwards NEG-OPEN or NEG-MSG reconciliation payloads to the vulnerable parser can be taken down by a single client message. Clients processing messages from malicious relays are also exposed.

This specific vulnerability affects builds with the default std feature enabled. Builds without std use a BTreeSet and do not perform the vulnerable preallocation.

A message-size limit alone does not prevent exploitation because the malicious payload can be only a few bytes long.

Credit

Discovered and fixed by Alex Gleason (https://github.com/alexgleason).

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0366: Vulnerability in pest_grammars
entry.summary: Stack overflow when parsing deeply nested input in pest_grammars
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0366

Stack overflow when parsing deeply nested input in pest_grammars
Reported

CVSS Score
3.3 LOW
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Local
Attack Complexity

Privileges Required
Low
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
Low
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
Patched
  • >=2.9.3
Affected Functions
Version
pest_grammars::json::JsonParser::parse
  • <2.9.3

Description

Impact

In affected versions, parsing deeply nested input with pest_grammars::json::JsonParser can exhaust the native stack and abort the hosting process. Applications that accept attacker-controlled JSON without suitable resource limits may therefore be vulnerable to denial of service.

The reported reproduction demonstrates this behavior with deeply nested JSON arrays. The nesting required to trigger an overflow depends on the platform, available stack space, and build configuration; there is no portable safe nesting threshold.

Patches

Upgrade to pest_grammars 2.9.3 or later.

Version 2.9.3 requires the updated pest runtime and includes regression tests for deeply nested JSON with the optional call budget disabled. Supported std builds automatically check available native stack headroom at parser checkpoints and return a handled stack limit reached error when insufficient space is detected. This protection operates independently of pest::set_call_limit(). See the 2.9.3 dependencies and deep-nesting regression tests.

These checks are best-effort. They do not provide universal stack-overflow protection, apply when stack bounds cannot be determined, or provide native-stack protection in no_std builds.

Workarounds and defense in depth

Applications unable to upgrade should reject excessive nesting before invoking the affected parser or configure a suitably conservative pest::set_call_limit() budget. A call budget is not a portable stack-depth guarantee.

Even after upgrading, applications parsing untrusted input should enforce workload-appropriate input, work, memory, and concurrency limits. Stack checks and call budgets do not enforce elapsed-time deadlines. Where a hard deadline or cancellation is required, use supervised parsing as described in the security policy: Parsing Untrusted Input.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0367: Vulnerability in zip
entry.summary: Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation
entry.content:

Insecure Preservation of SUID/SGID Bits during ZIP Extraction Leading to Potential Privilege Escalation

CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
Patched
  • >=9.0.0

Description

The zip crate preserves privileged Unix permission bits (SUID, SGID, and sticky bits) from ZIP external_attributes during extraction, instead of masking them to safe permission bits. If a privileged process (for example, root in an installer, CI/CD pipeline, or container build) extracts an attacker-controlled ZIP archive using ZipArchive::extract() or the stream extraction API, files can be created as setuid-root or setgid. This behavior allows the creation of SUID/SGID files during extraction, which can lead to local privilege escalation depending on the execution environment.

For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-vv5m-jxxh-4627

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0368: Vulnerability in zip
entry.summary: zip: `ZipArchive::extract` creates symbolic links whose attacker-controlled targets are outside the destination directory
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0368

zip: ZipArchive::extract creates symbolic links whose attacker-controlled targets are outside the destination directory
Reported
October 9, 2026
Issued
October 17, 2026
Package
zip (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • privilege-escalation
Keywords
#privilege-escalation #symlink
Aliases
  • GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26
Patched
  • >=9.0.0

Description

In zip 9.0.0-pre2, ZipArchive::extract creates a symbolic link from an archive entry after validating only the output entry path. The link target bytes are passed directly to the platform symlink API, so a malicious archive can create an entry inside the destination that resolves to an attacker-chosen path outside it. This behavior was verified on macOS and Linux. On either platform, a subsequent application read or write through that extracted entry accesses the external target with the extracting process's permissions.

For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-4v9h-p7m9-rh26

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.summary: Buffered application data sent to outer server after ECH rejection
entry.content:

Unaffected
  • <0.23.44

Description

When a server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), the client completes the handshake using the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the ECH config's public_name. At the end of that handshake, rustls encrypted and queued any application data buffered via ClientConnection::writer() before queueing the ech_required alert.

The application correctly receives Error::PeerIncompatible(ServerRejectedEncryptedClientHello), but the next write_tls() call (needed to send the alert) also sends the buffered application data. Plaintext meant for the inner server therefore goes to the client-facing server named by public_name.

That server is authenticated, so this is not exploitable by an unauthenticated party, but it violates RFC 9849 section 6.1.6, which requires the client to abort with ech_required "before sending any application data to the server".

This affects only clients that:

  • use EchMode::Enable (GREASE ECH is not affected),
  • write application data before the handshake completes, and
  • connect to a server that rejects their ECH config (for example, because it is stale).

The underlying ordering bug is older, but before 0.23.44 the client checked the server certificate against the inner server name rather than public_name, so certificate verification failed first and no data was sent.

Description

The built-in Brotli certificate decompressor (enabled by the non-default brotli crate feature) bounded the size of the decompressed output, but accepted a peer-selected history window. Brotli's large-window extension was enabled, so a five-byte header could cause an allocation of 1 GiB. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N
Patched

Description

The client recorded the server-selected key exchange group for each server name when processing the ServerHello, before the server was authenticated. This record is used to predict which key share to send in future ClientHellos to that server name.

A network attacker can answer one connection attempt with a ServerHello selecting X25519, and then close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry only an X25519 key share, while supported_groups still lists X25519MLKEM768 first. If the genuine server accepts that share rather than sending a HelloRetryRequest for its preferred hybrid group, the handshake completes with classical-only key exchange and no error. This persists for as long as the entry stays in the client's session store.

The impact is loss of post-quantum confidentiality for affected connections ("harvest now, decrypt later"). There is no key compromise and no authentication bypass.

The following are not affected:

  • connections to servers which send a HelloRetryRequest for their preferred group,
  • clients with resumption disabled (as nothing is stored), and
  • other server names.

This behaviour is discussed in draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction, so the practical impact depends largely on server policy.

Description

The neutralization that ammonia applied to animate and set was not applied to other forms of SVG animation, which can be used for XSS.

The following SVG will produce a link with a javascript scheme. If the user clicks this link, they will run it.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <a>
    <animateMotion attributeName="href" to="javascript:alert('SET_XSS')"></animateMotion>
    <text y="30">Click set</text>
  </a>
</svg>

Ammonia did not apply attribute filters based on attributeName, so the contents of the to, from, and values tags were not sanitized as URLs.

Applications that do not explicitly allow any of these tags should not be affected, since none are allowed by default.

This vulnerability was reported by ucsurf.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0345: Vulnerability in kuva
entry.summary: Untrusted labels can inject SVG attributes, CSS values, and terminal escape sequences
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0345

Untrusted labels can inject SVG attributes, CSS values, and terminal escape sequences
Reported
August 7, 2026
Issued
October 13, 2026
Package
kuva (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • format-injection
Keywords
#svg #xss #injection #ansi #escaping
Aliases
  • GHSA-3c48-9r95-hqhr
References
  • https://github.com/Psy-Fer/kuva/commit/2b53ceb796bbb0e9bb537836ad19faac53a51852
  • https://github.com/Psy-Fer/kuva/commit/2219f5931913f79f3b9be47690b8999a3d8b8bfb
  • https://github.com/Psy-Fer/kuva/commit/76049ff5133dfb796ba759c2c5e486779d3d30c5
  • https://github.com/Psy-Fer/kuva/releases/tag/v0.4.1
  • https://github.com/Psy-Fer/kuva/releases/tag/v0.3.1
Patched
  • >=0.3.1, <0.4.0
  • >=0.4.1
Unaffected
  • <0.1.5

Description

Affected versions of kuva wrote data-derived strings straight into rendered output without escaping them for the target format. Applications that plot untrusted input (column headers, category and group names, series labels) were affected in three places.

1. SVG attribute injection / stored XSS (CWE-79). When SVG interactivity was enabled via Layout::with_interactive, group and category labels were formatted directly into data-group and data-x attributes through the raw Primitive::GroupStart.extra_attrs string, which the SVG backend emitted verbatim. The backend's escaping helper covered text nodes and <title> but not attributes. A label containing a double quote could close the attribute and add another, for example an event handler. Opening the resulting SVG in a browser, or inlining it into an HTML page, executed the injected script. Reachable from scatter, line, bar, and strip plots, and from legends.

2. Unvalidated CSS and style attribute values (CWE-74). Color::Css wrote arbitrary strings into fill and stroke, stroke-dasharray was emitted raw from the public dash-pattern builders, and the SVG root font-family and fill plus the background rectangle fill were written raw from layout and theme configuration. Applications that forwarded user-supplied style values into the plotting API could have those values break out of the attribute they were written into.

3. Terminal escape sequence injection (CWE-150). TerminalBackend stored label characters unfiltered and emitted each one unconditionally when producing its ANSI string. Control characters in a label, including ESC, OSC sequences, and carriage returns, were written straight to the operator's terminal. Depending on the emulator this allows forged or misleading output, window title and clipboard manipulation, and reaching terminal emulator vulnerabilities that are triggered by escape sequences.

The fix routes every data-derived string through format-appropriate escaping. A single escape_attr helper XML-escapes &, <, >, ", and ', and is applied at each raw-attribute site: the extra_attrs interpolations, the Color::Css catch-all, and the SVG backend's stroke-dasharray, font-family, and background fill writes. TerminalBackend::set_char replaces control characters with U+FFFD before they enter the character grid, so one cell stays one column rather than the grid shifting, and the ANSI writer emits the grid unchanged.

Patched in 0.5.0, with backports to 0.4.1 for the 0.4.x line and 0.3.1 for users still on 0.1.5 through 0.3.0. No versions were yanked.

Users who cannot upgrade should sanitize labels before passing them to kuva, and avoid interactive SVG output for untrusted data.

Note that Scene::defs, Scene::scripts, and Primitive::GroupStart.extra_attrs remain raw escape hatches by design. They are documented as trusted-only and are not covered by this advisory; populating them from user data is equivalent to executing that data.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

Description

A crafted .zst input under 128 KB can force ruzstd to allocate several gigabytes at once, crashing the process with an out-of-memory condition. Since ruzstd is a decoder for untrusted input, a single small file is enough to take down anything decoding it.

The compressed size of a block was capped at 128 KB, but a compressed block's decompressed size was never checked against Block_Maximum_Size = min(Window_Size, 128 KiB) (RFC 8878). In execute_sequences the output was built with no running bound and no flush between blocks, so one block could expand to gigabytes — bypassing both the configured window-size limit and the block-by-block streaming that would otherwise release memory. (A related u32 counter overflow on such a block caused an additional panic.)

This is a denial of service only; memory access stays in bounds (no corruption, no RCE).

ruzstd is also built as a dependency of the Rust standard library via rustc-dep-of-std; in the toolchain it is used only to load zstd-compressed debug symbols, so the toolchain-side impact is limited.

Fixed in 0.9.1 (commit d3907c9), which enforces the per-block output bound. Upgrade to ruzstd >= 0.9.1.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.
